# The Lean layer's open debts

**GENERATED by [lean_debts.py](scripts/misc/lean_debts.py) from the layer itself, on 2026-09-29. Nothing here is edited by hand.** A row leaves this file when its `sorry` is discharged or its `native_decide` retired, so an entry standing here is an entry still owed. *Editing it by hand is the one way it can lie: a row deleted while the debt stands reappears on the next run, and a row added by hand never leaves.*

**Regenerate with `python3 scripts/misc/lean_debts.py`**, after `python3 scripts/misc/axiom_audit.py --json lean/axioms.json` when the second table is to move. *The first table is read from the sources, so it is as current as the last run of this script. The second is read from the audit and is as old as the audit.*

**105 numbered results carry no Lean proof** (the coverage debt, last section, which the lean loop works from).

Read from **1135 files**: **7 open `sorry`** across 7 of them, and **`native_decide` in 0 files**, tainting **1 declarations**.

## The compiler debt: proved by trusting the Lean compiler rather than the kernel

**These read as proved and are weaker than proved.** `native_decide` evaluates the claim with the compiled evaluator and the kernel takes the answer on trust, so the guarantee covers the compiler and its backend as well as the kernel. **The trust propagates**: every theorem importing one of these inherits it, which is why the base layer dominates the table.

*Retiring one is a derivation rather than a tactic swap.* Kernel arithmetic on `ℚ` reduces through `Rat.normalize`, which is exactly what the kernel will not unfold cheaply, so `decide` walls on these sums. **`norm_num` DOES NOT WALL, because it emits a certificate the kernel checks rather than asking the kernel to evaluate**, and [Sharp.lean](lean/HamiltonsCubic/Base/Sharp.lean) was retired entirely this way on 2026-09-20, four declarations including the layer's normalisation anchor. *A first version of this paragraph said `norm_num` walls too, which was a route recorded closed from one attempt.* **The unfold set is the work**: `Fin.sum_univ_six` rather than `Fin.sum_univ_succ`, so an index match meets literal indices instead of `Fin.succ` terms and reduces at all; `Matrix.cons_val_two`, `_three` and `_four` with `Matrix.vecHead` and `Matrix.vecTail`, so a `![...]` literal evaluates at a numeral; `Fin.ext_iff` so residual `Fin` equalities decide; and a raised `maxHeartbeats` with `simp`'s own `maxSteps` where the term is large, the config going BEFORE `only`. **The other route, proving the general-`n` statement and taking the fixed dimension as a corollary, removes the axiom AND strengthens the claim**, so it is the better one where the general statement is true and reachable.

**AND `native_decide` BUYS SPEED AS WELL AS CONVENIENCE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES A RETIREMENT COST SOMETHING.** *The compiled evaluator settles a closed rational computation in milliseconds where the kernel grinds through every step of it*, so a retirement can turn a module that built in seconds into one that takes minutes, **and every later build pays that, not just the cycle that made the change.** *A retirement reported only as `#print axioms` clean has reported half of it.* **SO TIME THE MODULE BEFORE AND AFTER, AND PUT BOTH NUMBERS IN THE COMMIT.** Where the cost is large the answer is usually a better proof rather than a reverted one: **the general-`n` route is fast** because it replaces a fixed-dimension expansion with a structural argument, and a brute `simp` over every entry at a raised heartbeat limit is the shape that gets expensive.

**Where the taint lands, by namespace**: `HamiltonsCubic.Base` carries 1. *The namespace a declaration ends up in is not the file the tactic was written in, so the table below is the work list and this line is its consequence.*

## The hypothesis debt: closed claims stated, passed round, and proved nowhere

**This is the kind that hides best.** A `sorry` announces itself and a `native_decide` shows in the axiom set. *A `Prop` defined once, taken as a hypothesis by several results and proved nowhere reads as ordinary machinery*: every file naming it type-checks, the build is green, and the axiom audit comes back clean, because **a conditional theorem really is proved**. What is unproved is its antecedent, and nothing else in this repository counts those.

**A ROW WITH NO CONSUMERS IS NOT THEREBY DEAD WEIGHT, AND THIS TABLE CANNOT TELL A GOAL FROM AN ABANDONED HYPOTHESIS.** *A statement of the problem has exactly this shape: defined once, taken by nothing, concluded by nothing.* **So read the definition before working a consumerless row**, since the cheapest-looking entry here is the one whose deletion costs most.

**Keeping such a claim as a hypothesis rather than an `axiom` is the right call and is not what is owed.** *A binder is visible to every reader and every caller, where an `axiom` is visible only to `#print axioms`.* **What is owed is that each of these is either proved or retired**, since every result taking one is conditional until then.

**A CONSUMER HERE IS A FILE WITH A BINDER.** *This column read `if the name appears in the file` until 2026-09-18, and an audit against the tree found SIX of the seven rows it produced wrong, in both directions: prose mentions counted as consumers, theorems CONCLUDING the claim counted as consumers, binders in the defining file dropped by an explicit exclusion, and two different `Prop`s of the same name collapsed into one row.* **A prose mention is a reader's signpost and a binder is a debt**, and only the second is counted below.

**A claim with a CONDITIONAL producer keeps its row.** *A theorem concluding the claim from hypotheses of its own moves the debt rather than closing it, and the producer column says where it moved to.*
